_comment: Bible section 8 loop: Town -> Explore -> Combat -> Rewards -> Town -> Sleep -> Morning Autosave. Towns are safe; wilderness areas roll encounters.
flavour: The path is quiet.
Wind moves through the grass and nothing follows it.
You find old tracks, already filling with rain.
Something watched you pass, then thought better of it.
A cold draught rises from somewhere below.
You rest a moment. Nothing comes.
A caravan bell sounds somewhere beyond the next ridge.
Fresh bootprints cross the road, then vanish at bare stone.
Smoke on the horizon belongs to a town, probably.
A weathered shrine holds three new offerings.
You share the road with merchants until the next turning.
Far-off mining hammers keep a patient rhythm.
Cloud shadows race you across the open ground.
Someone has repaired the trail marker since yesterday.

areas.name: Ashvale
areas.description: A small town built around a very old well. People stay because leaving is harder.

areas.name: The Greenfields
areas.description: Long grass, low hills, and more wildlife than the farmers would like.

areas.name: The Old Road
areas.description: The paving stones are good. The people using them are not.

ancestry_actions.name: Share the road
ancestry_actions.description: At the old milestones, choose whether your heritage is defined by community or self-reliance. This decision cannot be undone.
ancestry_actions.outcome: You leave supplies and maps for those who will travel after you.

ancestry_actions.name: Walk your own trail
ancestry_actions.description: At the old milestones, choose whether your heritage is defined by community or self-reliance. This decision cannot be undone.
ancestry_actions.outcome: You mark a private route and trust your own judgment to carry it forward.

areas.name: The Hollow
areas.description: A cave that goes down further than the town admits.

areas.name: The Sunken Shrine
areas.description: Someone built this to keep something in, and then stopped visiting.

ancestry_actions.name: Gather the voices at the well
ancestry_actions.description: Return to an ancient shrine and bind the many lessons of humanity into a single deliberate path.
ancestry_actions.outcome: The old well reflects a hundred human lives. Their contradictions become your strength.

areas.name: The Cinder Road
areas.description: Black milestones lead west through grass that never stopped smouldering.

areas.name: Emberwatch
areas.description: A walled market town where every roof carries a rain barrel and every citizen knows the fire bell.

ancestry_actions.name: Honor both houses
ancestry_actions.description: At Emberwatch’s old bridge, choose whether you honour inheritance or build a third path between it. This decision cannot be undone.
ancestry_actions.outcome: You carry two histories without allowing either to erase the other.

ancestry_actions.name: Choose a third path
ancestry_actions.description: At Emberwatch’s old bridge, choose whether you honour inheritance or build a third path between it. This decision cannot be undone.
ancestry_actions.outcome: You refuse inherited expectations and define belonging for yourself.

ancestry_actions.name: Save the luck
ancestry_actions.description: At Emberwatch, choose whether luck is something to hoard or something made by helping others. This decision cannot be undone.
ancestry_actions.outcome: You keep the fortunate token for the moment only you can survive.

ancestry_actions.name: Share the luck
ancestry_actions.description: At Emberwatch, choose whether luck is something to hoard or something made by helping others. This decision cannot be undone.
ancestry_actions.outcome: You pass the token on and trust good fortune to return another way.

areas.name: Mosswood
areas.description: Ancient trees drink warm rain while paths rearrange behind travellers.

areas.name: The Glassmarsh
areas.description: Still pools mirror the sky too perfectly, even when something moves beneath them.

ancestry_actions.name: Rewrite the pact
ancestry_actions.description: At the glassmarsh mirrors, choose whether to amend your inherited pact or leave every promise unanswered. This decision cannot be undone.
ancestry_actions.outcome: You shape the terms of your inheritance instead of denying its existence.

ancestry_actions.name: Walk unbound
ancestry_actions.description: At the glassmarsh mirrors, choose whether to amend your inherited pact or leave every promise unanswered. This decision cannot be undone.
ancestry_actions.outcome: You leave every inherited promise behind and claim a harder freedom.

ancestry_actions.name: Keep the pack
ancestry_actions.description: In the Glassmarsh, choose whether your instincts are strongest in a pack or in the freedom to roam alone. This decision cannot be undone.
ancestry_actions.outcome: You promise to lend your strength to those who run beside you.

ancestry_actions.name: Follow the lone trail
ancestry_actions.description: In the Glassmarsh, choose whether your instincts are strongest in a pack or in the freedom to roam alone. This decision cannot be undone.
ancestry_actions.outcome: You trust the solitary instinct that keeps you alive between territories.

ancestry_actions.name: Preserve the pattern
ancestry_actions.description: At the Glassmarsh reflections, choose whether fate is a pattern to preserve or a thread to cut. This decision cannot be undone.
ancestry_actions.outcome: You honour the pattern that carried your people through countless storms.

ancestry_actions.name: Cut a new thread
ancestry_actions.description: At the Glassmarsh reflections, choose whether fate is a pattern to preserve or a thread to cut. This decision cannot be undone.
ancestry_actions.outcome: You accept the risk of a future no elder has already woven.

areas.name: The Drowned Archive
areas.description: Stone shelves descend into black water, their books whispering through sealed covers.

ancestry_actions.name: Keep the old verse
ancestry_actions.description: In the drowned archive, decide whether memory must be preserved exactly or allowed to change with the living. This decision cannot be undone.
ancestry_actions.outcome: You preserve the original cadence exactly as the elders taught it.

ancestry_actions.name: Compose a new verse
ancestry_actions.description: In the drowned archive, decide whether memory must be preserved exactly or allowed to change with the living. This decision cannot be undone.
ancestry_actions.outcome: You answer the old song with a living verse of your own.

ancestry_actions.name: Claim the debt
ancestry_actions.description: At the drowned archive, choose whether infernal power is a debt to collect or a burden to carry. This decision cannot be undone.
ancestry_actions.outcome: You accept the sharp certainty of the old court’s bargain.

ancestry_actions.name: Break the debt
ancestry_actions.description: At the drowned archive, choose whether infernal power is a debt to collect or a burden to carry. This decision cannot be undone.
ancestry_actions.outcome: You refuse to let an ancestor’s bargain define your hunger.

ancestry_actions.name: Preserve the judgment
ancestry_actions.description: At the Drowned Archive, choose whether ancient memory should judge the living or teach them mercy. This decision cannot be undone.
ancestry_actions.outcome: You keep the old verdicts intact, trusting memory over sentiment.

ancestry_actions.name: Choose mercy
ancestry_actions.description: At the Drowned Archive, choose whether ancient memory should judge the living or teach them mercy. This decision cannot be undone.
ancestry_actions.outcome: You let the past instruct the present without ruling it.

areas.name: Stonehaven
areas.description: A mining city carved into a cliff, loud with lifts, chisels, and shift bells.

areas.name: The Red Pass
areas.description: Iron dust stains the mountain road and every boot that survives it.

ancestry_actions.name: Temper by tradition
ancestry_actions.description: At the Red Pass forge-stones, choose whether tradition or invention should shape the next generation of craft. This decision cannot be undone.
ancestry_actions.outcome: You use the old measurements, accepting the discipline they demand.

ancestry_actions.name: Temper by innovation
ancestry_actions.description: At the Red Pass forge-stones, choose whether tradition or invention should shape the next generation of craft. This decision cannot be undone.
ancestry_actions.outcome: You alter the pattern and accept responsibility for what follows.

ancestry_actions.name: Sing for conquest
ancestry_actions.description: At the Red Pass, choose whether your war song belongs to conquest or protection. This decision cannot be undone.
ancestry_actions.outcome: You accept that strength must sometimes take the ground it needs.

ancestry_actions.name: Sing for protection
ancestry_actions.description: At the Red Pass, choose whether your war song belongs to conquest or protection. This decision cannot be undone.
ancestry_actions.outcome: You make strength a shelter for those who cannot yet stand alone.

areas.name: The Singing Mines
areas.description: Blue crystal veins vibrate with every footstep, building toward a song nobody wants to finish.

ancestry_actions.name: Carry it alone
ancestry_actions.description: In the Singing Mines, choose whether your strength is measured by burdens carried alone or shared with others. This decision cannot be undone.
ancestry_actions.outcome: You prove the solitary endurance your ancestors prized.

ancestry_actions.name: Share the burden
ancestry_actions.description: In the Singing Mines, choose whether your strength is measured by burdens carried alone or shared with others. This decision cannot be undone.
ancestry_actions.outcome: You prove that strength can include asking another to stand beside you.

areas.name: Storm Plateau
areas.description: Open stone rises above the cloud line beneath a sky that never stops choosing targets.

ancestry_actions.name: Publish the design
ancestry_actions.description: On the storm plateau, choose whether a dangerous invention should be shared freely or safeguarded. This decision cannot be undone.
ancestry_actions.outcome: You trust many hands and many minds to improve the invention.

ancestry_actions.name: Guard the design
ancestry_actions.description: On the storm plateau, choose whether a dangerous invention should be shared freely or safeguarded. This decision cannot be undone.
ancestry_actions.outcome: You keep the dangerous details from those who would use them carelessly.

areas.name: Skyreach
areas.description: Rope bridges and white towers cling to the peak above an ocean of cloud.

areas.name: The Cloud Ruins
areas.description: Roofless halls drift in and out of fog, patrolled by machines older than the mountain.

ancestry_actions.name: Answer the sky-song
ancestry_actions.description: Sing the recovered fragment beneath the cloud ruins and let it become more than an echo of the past.
ancestry_actions.outcome: The ruins answer in harmonics older than any tower, and your ancestry technique resonates with them.

ancestry_actions.name: Name your horizon
ancestry_actions.description: At the cloud ruins, speak the name you have chosen for yourself into the open sky.
ancestry_actions.outcome: Wind carries your chosen name through the ruins. No lineage can speak over it again.

ancestry_actions.name: Serve the brood
ancestry_actions.description: Among the cloud ruins, choose whether your draconic oath is service to a brood or mastery of yourself. This decision cannot be undone.
ancestry_actions.outcome: You bind your strength to the safety and honour of your people.

ancestry_actions.name: Master the self
ancestry_actions.description: Among the cloud ruins, choose whether your draconic oath is service to a brood or mastery of yourself. This decision cannot be undone.
ancestry_actions.outcome: You swear that blood is a beginning, not a command.

ancestry_actions.name: Lay the road table
ancestry_actions.description: At the cloud ruins, set a table for strangers and prove that home can travel with you.
ancestry_actions.outcome: A meal shared above the clouds makes even ancient ruins feel briefly like home.

ancestry_actions.name: Command the storm
ancestry_actions.description: At the cloud ruins, choose whether an element is mastered through control or through surrender to its nature. This decision cannot be undone.
ancestry_actions.outcome: You impose shape and discipline on the elemental force within.

ancestry_actions.name: Ride the storm
ancestry_actions.description: At the cloud ruins, choose whether an element is mastered through control or through surrender to its nature. This decision cannot be undone.
ancestry_actions.outcome: You learn to move with elemental change rather than resisting it.

areas.name: The Obsidian Gate
areas.description: A black arch frames a sunrise from somewhere else. Something stands between here and morning.

ancestry_actions.name: Strike the first anvil
ancestry_actions.description: At the Obsidian Gate, awaken the memory of the first forge without repeating its oldest mistakes.
ancestry_actions.outcome: A single strike rings through the gate like a forge bell, hardening your resolve and technique.

ancestry_actions.name: Crown the scale
ancestry_actions.description: Face the Obsidian Gate and turn inherited pride into an oath you can actually uphold.
ancestry_actions.outcome: The gate drinks the echo of your roar and returns it as a disciplined, skybound power.

ancestry_actions.name: Speak the unburning name
ancestry_actions.description: At the Obsidian Gate, strip an inherited title of its power and decide what remains beneath it.
ancestry_actions.outcome: Ash rises but does not consume you. Your technique answers a name no court can own.

ancestry_actions.name: Open the door between
ancestry_actions.description: At the Obsidian Gate, close the door others opened in your name—or walk through it on your own terms.
ancestry_actions.outcome: The gate reveals a threshold within your own blood. You cross it without surrendering yourself.

ancestry_actions.name: Mark the unfenced trail
ancestry_actions.description: At the Obsidian Gate, claim a wild path that no fence, banner, or hunter can close.
ancestry_actions.outcome: Your scent carries across the black stone. The wild recognizes you as neither prey nor captive.

ancestry_actions.name: Raise the free banner
ancestry_actions.description: Raise a banner at the Obsidian Gate that carries strength without repeating old chains.
ancestry_actions.outcome: Your banner catches a hard wind above the gate. Its weight becomes purpose instead of burden.

ancestry_actions.name: Turn the impossible key
ancestry_actions.description: At the Obsidian Gate, assemble a device everyone calls impossible and prove them delightfully wrong.
ancestry_actions.outcome: The device hums once, then opens a pattern in the gate that only a gnomish mind would notice.

ancestry_actions.name: Join the confluence
ancestry_actions.description: At the Obsidian Gate, let every element in your blood meet without one consuming the others.
ancestry_actions.outcome: Fire, wind, stone, and tide answer together. Your technique finds the rhythm between them.

ancestry_actions.name: Set the peak within
ancestry_actions.description: At the Obsidian Gate, stand beneath a weight no one else can lift and discover the peak inside yourself.
ancestry_actions.outcome: The gate’s weight presses down, then becomes part of your stance instead of breaking it.

ancestry_actions.name: Wear the serpent crown
ancestry_actions.description: At the Obsidian Gate, claim a crown of memory without allowing it to close around your throat.
ancestry_actions.outcome: The old crown coils around your thoughts, then loosens when it finds you are not its prisoner.

ancestry_actions.name: Weave tomorrow
ancestry_actions.description: At the Obsidian Gate, weave one final thread into a future that remains yours to change.
ancestry_actions.outcome: Silk catches on black stone, forming a path that did not exist until you chose to make it.

areas.name: Ironveil Approach
areas.description: The road to Ironveil winds through petrified forest, where ancient trees stand as stone sentinels.

areas.name: Ironveil
areas.description: A fortress-city carved into a mountainside, seat of the Iron Covenant faction. The walls hum with ancient wards.

areas.name: Ashen Wastes
areas.description: A blasted landscape where an ancient battle scorched the earth. Embers still glow beneath the ash.

areas.name: Cinder Depths
areas.description: Volcanic caverns where magma rivers flow between obsidian pillars. The heat is oppressive.

areas.name: Sunken Citadel
areas.description: A drowned fortress rising from a black lake. The water is unnaturally still and cold.

areas.name: Abyssal Halls
areas.description: The deepest chambers of the Sunken Citadel, where reality thins and the void seeps through.

areas.name: Molten Sanctum
areas.description: The heart of the volcano, where an ancient dragon once forged weapons of terrible power.

areas.name: The Void Throne
areas.description: A chamber at the edge of reality, where the Void Sovereign sits upon a throne of nothing.

areas.name: Celestial Crossing
areas.description: A bridge of fallen stars spans the void between oblivion and eternity, each step echoing with half-remembered oaths.
flavour: Starlight pools like water at your feet.
The air smells of ozone and old vows.

areas.name: Celestial Archives
areas.description: A library-city suspended in starlight, where chroniclers etch the names of those who dare ascend.
flavour: Scrolls float, turning their own pages.
You hear whispers of futures that never happened.

areas.name: Astral Rift
areas.description: Reality frays here; constellations bleed into one another and the ground forgets to be solid.
flavour: Gravity inverts briefly, then apologizes.
You see your own back, walking ahead.

areas.name: Abyssal Maw
areas.description: A chasm that breathes, inhaling light and exhaling things that should not be named.
flavour: The maw exhales, and your torch gutters without wind.
Something vast shifts below, and the whole chasm shudders.

areas.name: Throne of Ascension
areas.description: At the apex of all tiers, a single throne awaits. It is empty, and yet it watches.
flavour: Every step you ever took led here, whether you knew it or not.
The throne is warm, as if just vacated.

shops.name: Celestial Outfitters
shops.description: Star-forged gear for those nearing godhood.

shops.name: Archive Exchange
shops.description: Knowledge and relics traded for ascendant essence.

npcs.name: Mara
npcs.description: Runs the inn. Has run it for a long time.
dialogue: Bed's the same price as yesterday. So's the porridge.
You look like the road's been arguing with you.
Stay as long as you like. People usually don't.
The well's older than the town. Don't drop anything in it.

npcs.name: Dorn
npcs.description: The smith. Speaks mostly in prices.
dialogue: Bring me steel and I'll make it worth carrying.
That edge is a disgrace. Give it here.
Everything breaks. Question is how loudly.
Cheap armour costs more. You'll see.

npcs.name: Iven
npcs.description: Reads too much and says so.
dialogue: The shrine predates the town. Nobody finds that interesting but me.
Seven tiers, the old texts say. Most never pass the second.
Mastery isn't talent. It's repetition nobody watched.
If you find anything written down out there, bring it back intact.

npcs.name: Warden Hela
npcs.description: Keeps the walls staffed and the fire buckets full.
dialogue: The bell rings once for a drill, twice for fire, continuously for fools.
Emberwatch was rebuilt six times. We kept the name to save paint.
West road is open. Safe would be a stronger word.

npcs.name: Pell
npcs.description: An alchemist whose eyebrows are recent replacements.
dialogue: Green bottle heals. Blue bottle helps magic. Striped bottle is lunch.
I need marsh ichor. Need is perhaps too gentle a word.
If it bubbles clockwise, leave the room calmly.

npcs.name: Senn
npcs.description: Draws maps in erasable charcoal for practical reasons.
dialogue: Mosswood moved two paths again last night.
Stonehaven is west, down, and louder than expected.
A blank place on a map is not an invitation. Usually.

npcs.name: Reeve Marta
npcs.description: Runs Stonehaven by ledger, whistle, and inexhaustible disapproval.
dialogue: Visitors sign in. Heroes sign twice.
The mine is singing in a new key. Nobody likes it.
If Tala says a tunnel is safe, it is. If Orren says it, ask Tala.

npcs.name: Joss
npcs.description: A lift operator who has seen every depth and recommends none.
dialogue: Down is easy. Coming back is skilled work.
Don't whistle underground. The crystals answer.
Colossus used to guard us. Pronouns changed somewhere along the way.

npcs.name: Ada
npcs.description: Catalogues runes by effect, age, and likelihood of explosion.
dialogue: Old runes command. New runes negotiate.
Bring me anything that glows without heat.
The plateau inscriptions all point upward. Grammatically, not geographically.

npcs.name: Lume
npcs.description: Records weather, ruins, and every traveller who returns from either.
dialogue: History is thinner up here. The wind takes loose pages.
The Obsidian Gate predates the mountain road.
Morning through the gate arrives from the wrong direction.

npcs.name: Fenn
npcs.description: Trusts rope more than stone and people less than either.
dialogue: Every bridge is a promise with knots.
Check the wind, then check it again after it lies.
Falling is free. Everything before it costs.

npcs.name: Abbess Sol
npcs.description: Tends a roofless chapel facing the gate.
dialogue: Light is not goodness. Fire teaches that early.
The thing at the gate calls itself dawn. Names are claims.
Go prepared. Faith is not a substitute for armour.

npcs.name: Elder Amariel
npcs.description: An elven gardener keeping one impossible silver sapling alive in a fire town.
dialogue: Some trees grow toward sunlight. This one grows toward memory.
Lethira lost something in Mosswood. The wood found it first.
I came for one season. That was eighty-three years ago.
Emberwatch ash makes excellent roses. Angry roses, but excellent.

npcs.name: Nima Crossroads
npcs.description: A half-elven courier who knows which roads accept which names.
dialogue: A letter arrives faster when it contains an apology.
Two families taught me two ways to get lost.
Ashvale is where roads come to reconsider.
I deliver secrets sealed. Reading them costs extra and my self-respect.

npcs.name: Thane Dorrim
npcs.description: Keeper of an erased clan ledger and Brokk's least patient uncle.
dialogue: A name removed from stone leaves a louder space.
Brokk hears songs because he refuses sensible silence.
Our ledger has one clean cut. History is rarely that tidy.
I do not hold grudges. I archive them.

npcs.name: Mother Sable
npcs.description: A demon advocate offering free counsel and terrifyingly precise tea.
dialogue: Never sign your true name. Initials have saved kingdoms.
Veyra mistakes escape for absolution. She needs both.
Demons do not all lie. That rumour was started by honest lawyers.
Tea is a contract: patience in exchange for flavour.

npcs.name: Keth Cloudscar
npcs.description: A dragonkin historian reconstructing the first gate oath from scorched scales.
dialogue: Scales preserve heat and, sometimes, testimony.
Rhazek inherited an oath with half the verbs missing.
The gate was sealed against dawn, not darkness.
History written in fire is difficult to alphabetise.

npcs.name: Siv Quickpaw
npcs.description: A fox-eared salvager with excellent balance and flexible definitions of abandoned.
dialogue: If the ruin wanted it, it should have held tighter.
My tail is for balance, not public commentary.
Sentinels hate bells. I carry seven.
I found a crown yesterday. Turned out to be plumbing.

npcs.name: Thrakk Warbringer
npcs.description: An orcish weapons merchant who believes every problem has an axe-shaped solution.
dialogue: You want weapon? Thrakk has weapon. Many weapons.
This axe killed three trolls. The trolls were not impressed.
Orc steel is honest steel. It breaks before it bends.
Buy something or fight me. Both are honourable.
My prices are fair. My temper is not.
You look like someone who needs a bigger sword.

npcs.name: Cogsworth Tinkerton
npcs.description: A gnome merchant whose wares occasionally tick, whirr, or explode.
dialogue: Welcome to Cogsworth's Curios! Satisfaction guaranteed* (*some conditions apply).
This device does something. I'm just not sure what yet.
All sales final. Especially the explosive ones.
My latest invention! It makes tea AND predicts the weather. Mostly.
Have you tried percussive maintenance? It works 30% of the time.
I once sold a clock that ran backwards. Customer loved it. Said it gave him more time.

npcs.name: Butterbur Goodbody
npcs.description: A halfling innkeeper whose cooking is legendary and whose gossip is better.
dialogue: Welcome, welcome! Have you eaten? You look thin.
My grandmother's pie recipe. Secret ingredient is love. And lard. Mostly lard.
The rooms are clean, the beds are soft, and the breakfast is mandatory.
I know everyone's business. It's not gossip if it's true.
Halfling hospitality: you'll leave fuller than you arrived.
Second breakfast is at eleven. Elevenses is at ten. Don't be late.

npcs.name: Zephyr Stormcaller
npcs.description: An air genasi weather mage who reads the winds like others read books.
dialogue: The winds speak of change. They always do.
I don't predict weather. I negotiate with it.
My mood affects the local barometric pressure. Fair warning.
Air genasi don't get grounded. We get... redirected.
Tomorrow will be windy with a chance of existential dread.
I once calmed a hurricane. It was very apologetic afterwards.

npcs.name: Granite Heart
npcs.description: A goliath stonemason whose sculptures are said to move when no one watches.
dialogue: Stone remembers. I just help it speak.
My chisel is sharp. My patience is sharper.
Every boulder is a statue waiting to be freed.
Goliaths measure worth in deeds, not words. So let me work.
This sculpture took three years. The mountain took three million.
I don't carve stone. I convince it to be something else.

npcs.name: Ophidia Scalesinger
npcs.description: A lamia historian whose memory stretches back centuries.
dialogue: I remember when this cave was a cathedral. And before that, a sea.
History is not past. It is simply elsewhere.
My scales carry the stories of a thousand years.
Young ones always rush. I have learned patience from the stone.
The old magics still whisper, if you know how to listen.
I once debated a dragon about the nature of time. We both won.

npcs.name: Spinner Fateweaver
npcs.description: An arachne weaver whose tapestries are said to show glimpses of possible futures.
dialogue: Every thread is a choice. Every pattern, a consequence.
I weave what might be, not what will be. The difference matters.
My silk catches more than flies. It catches moments.
Eight eyes see eight truths. Which one do you want?
This tapestry shows your future. Or perhaps your past. Time is flexible.
I don't predict fate. I illustrate it.

npcs.name: Commander Vex
npcs.description: The stern commander of Ironveil, scarred from decades of border wars.
dialogue: Ironveil stands because we do not bend.
The Void Sovereign grows stronger. We must act before it's too late.
Every soldier under my command has earned their place. Have you?
The walls are old. Older than the city. Older than the mountain.
I've buried too many good people. I won't bury more if I can help it.
You want to help? Good. We need every blade we can get.

npcs.name: Artificer Zara
npcs.description: A gnome artificer whose workshop fills half a city block with humming machinery.
dialogue: This machine? Oh, it only explodes on Tuesdays. Today is... not Tuesday.
I've been working on a device that can fold space. It currently folds my laundry instead.
The Void Throne interests me. Scientifically. Not existentially. Mostly.
My last apprentice was very talented. Unfortunately, so was the explosion.
Ironveil's wards are my design. They hum at exactly 440 Hz. Perfect A.
You want enchantments? I want test subjects. Fair trade?

npcs.name: Chronicler Thon
npcs.description: An ancient lamia who has recorded every event in Ironveil's history.
dialogue: I remember when this mountain was a hill. Time is a funny thing.
The Void Sovereign is not new. It has waited since before the first city.
History is not just dates and battles. It's the smell of bread on a winter morning.
I've written four hundred volumes. I'm running out of shelves.
The old texts speak of a weapon that can seal the void. If they're not lying.
You remind me of someone. Someone who didn't come back. Be careful.
